newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks fall by lunch, banks lead decline.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks fall by lunch, banks lead decline.

text.p: Thai stocks fell by the midday break after active unloading of finance and bank issues, brokers said on Tuesday.
The SET index retreated 5.60 points to 557.75 on thin 1.03 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index dropped 0.45 to 40.44.

"Selling of finance and bank shares led the market fall this morning," said one local broker. "Investors were sidelined by lingering worries about finance company health and bearish earning prospects of most major banks."
Declines led advances 171 to 41 with 68 issues remained unchanged.
Tightened liquidity and rising short-term baht interest rates also hurt the market as investors shifted funds to the money market to earn higher returns, brokers said.
Finance and bank sectors fell 1.80 and 1.72 percent respectively. The two counters accounted for nearly 40 percent of the morning trade.
Finance One topped the active list, losing 0.50 baht to 5.80. It resumed trading after a three-month suspension last Friday, -- Anuchit Nguyen (662) 652-0642
